reason: The first predecessor-boundary helper incorrectly qualified coalesce through pg_catalog; the test helper was corrected before evidence runs.
The independent predecessor comparison exposed that Down had not restored the legacy function ACLs; the product migration was corrected.
The first test counted a broader privilege surface (50) instead of the exact predecessor StageRights contract (41); the comparison now constructs and checks the exact predecessor signature/role set.
The post-Down legacy prepare smoke test initially expected ExistingMatch on a fresh reservation; the actual and correct legacy result is InProgress.

The unchanged historical test uses exact Assert.ThrowsAsync<InvalidOperationException> while production has long thrown the intentional RawIngressProviderCapabilityUnavailableException subtype. The candidate weakening was reverted; this unrelated baseline test is not cited as OpenBao evidence.
Renaming the sole required predecessor activate-body restore made the Down post-guard fail with OPENBAO_REPRESENTATION_DOWN_BODY_MISMATCH for the exact activate signature.
Changing one byte in the restored activate body made the exact pg_get_functiondef/prosrc boundary comparison fail.
Removing the legacy prepare grant made the exact predecessor ACL dictionary comparison fail for the custody-encryptor role.
Mapping OpenBaoTransportException back to CorruptOrUnverifiable made the taxonomy assertion fail: expected Unavailable, actual CorruptOrUnverifiable.
Measured the current provider behavior before tightening assertions: wrong context, tampered ciphertext and deleted key each produced OpenBaoTransportException status 400, non-transient.
Disabling the ExistingMatch lookup branch reached the wrap-throwing observer and failed with ACTIVE_REPLAY_MUST_NOT_WRAP_OR_CREATE_A_DEK_CANDIDATE.

Removing associated_data only from decrypt caused the valid positive unwrap to fail with OpenBaoTransportException before the negative assertions; this is the mechanically correct result for ciphertext originally encrypted with AAD.
Replacing the context contribution with a constant on both wrap and unwrap made wrong-context decrypt succeed; the exact ThrowsAsync assertion failed with no exception thrown.
